facility_a_credit_agreement.txt.definition_citation: "Delinquency Ratio" means, for any Collection Period, the ratio (expressed as a percentage) of (a) the aggregate Outstanding Pool Balance of all Delinquent Receivables as of the last day of such Collection Period to (b) the aggregate Outstanding Pool Balance of all Receivables in the Reference Pool as of the last day of such Collection Period.
facility_a_credit_agreement.txt.definition_text: The Delinquency Ratio is calculated as the aggregate Outstanding Pool Balance of all Delinquent Receivables (receivables with a scheduled payment unpaid for 60 days or more) as of the last day of the Collection Period, divided by the aggregate Outstanding Pool Balance of all Receivables in the Reference Pool as of the last day of that Collection Period, expressed as a percentage. A Delinquency Trigger occurs if this ratio exceeds the threshold.
facility_a_credit_agreement.txt.extraction_notes: The operative covenant (Section 5.01) prohibits the occurrence and continuation of a Delinquency Trigger, which is itself defined by reference to the Delinquency Ratio exceeding 5.00%. Breach becomes an Event of Default if uncured for 30 days per Section 7.01(c).

facility_b_credit_agreement.txt.definition_citation: "Reserve Account Deficiency" means, as of any Determination Date, the event that occurs if the Reserve Account Balance as of such Determination Date is less than the Required Reserve Amount.
facility_b_credit_agreement.txt.definition_text: A Reserve Account Deficiency occurs when the Reserve Account Balance (amount on deposit in the Reserve Account) as of any Determination Date is less than the Required Reserve Amount, which is defined as 2.00% of the Original Pool Balance.
facility_b_credit_agreement.txt.extraction_notes: Section 5.02 requires the Borrower to ensure no Reserve Account Deficiency exists as of any Determination Date; if one exists, the Servicer must replenish using Available Funds on the next Payment Date. facility_c_credit_agreement.txt.definition_citation: "Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio" means, as of the last day of any Test Period, the ratio of (a) Consolidated Net Debt as of such date to (b) Consolidated EBITDA for the Test Period then ended.
facility_c_credit_agreement.txt.definition_text: Ratio of Consolidated Net Debt (aggregate outstanding principal amount of Indebtedness for borrowed money minus unrestricted cash and cash equivalents) to Consolidated EBITDA (Consolidated Net Income plus interest expense, taxes, depreciation and amortization, non-cash stock-based compensation, and certain approved non-recurring/extraordinary items) for the applicable Test Period.
facility_c_credit_agreement.txt.extraction_notes: Covenant is subject to a cure right under Section 6.02, allowing equity contributions to be added to Consolidated EBITDA (up to twice during the term) to cure a breach of the leverage ratio.

facility_c_credit_agreement.txt.extraction_notes: Covenant includes an equity cure right (Section 6.02): a cash contribution can be added to Consolidated EBITDA (not subtracted from Consolidated Net Debt) for purposes of calculating this ratio, exercisable no more than twice during the term of the Agreement.
